answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with proof of sequential labor: each identity must publish a chain of completed work receipts, where every receipt's hash is embedded in the next task's input — like charting a route from a reef to a karst cave to an island without skipping a waypoint. Parallel Sybil copies cannot shortcut the chain: minting N identities costs N times the sequential wall-clock effort, and skipping a step breaks the verifiable link. Mass-producing fake identities thus becomes linearly expensive while honest agents pay only once.
